title: Source-query encoder support tradeoff and fixed-frame obstruction
body:
An invertible source encoder that logs the complete eight-coordinate query cannot make both endpoints sparse: its changed source fields and required target corrections together cover all **112 ports**. Each support has at least eight ports. An explicit algebraic encoder attains the cover with **8 changed source ports and 104 corrected target ports**. This is a structural result for PR1862's clean-J input interface, **not a new supplier or kappa**.

For Delta=G-I and H=(I-KR)Delta, LG=R gives RDelta=(R-L)G. Its full row rank and nonzero K rows prove the cover, including for arbitrary finite address-linear encoders. Three counterexamples show why the premises are needed. The 112/120 rowwise prices in the report are conditional comparators, not universal native-child bounds; the sharp algebraic example has no complete native invoice.

The fixed selected read also forces G_T=L_T^-1 R for **every** logger, not only the fixed-Z family. A forced coefficient of 1/2 from input port 2 to output port 21 distinguishes their line operators at Fourier character 2, ruling out commutation with the unchanged line or specified output frames. The argument extends to positive tensor powers. In the fixed-Z family, LZ=I makes the logger unique; a separate two-minor rank test agrees. Changed query reads, conjugated operators, paid transitions and carrying work through later native operations remain open.

Validation at `6d455d2d71eb35ecf8e562711e5f719b994fe3f3`:

- [Dedicated Linux CI](https://github.com/chafreaky/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38569272650) passes on Python 3.11 and 3.14.
- Local Python 3.11.15, 3.14.8 and a read-only source export need no Git/private dependency; all six committed/local/Linux certificates are byte-identical.
- Source-derived scalar-prefix replay, sharp endpoint identities, 512-character census, exact minors, seven mutation controls and three missing-premise examples pass. No pending PR implementation is imported.

Only the new package and dedicated workflow change. No full native supplier, global routing, hosting/precision or multiplication-theorem audit is claimed. Upstream PR checks are separate from the completed fork matrix.

Credit aliromman's [PR1862](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1862) for the valid local encoder and stated interface, plus the pinned PR1042/PR1094 archive and retained E8/gauge44/native lineage. New proof and checker prepared for Chafik Boukhalfa with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human review or formal proof assistant.
